comments.text: Set the VIC raster compare from A, acknowledge its interrupt, and write X and Y to the low and high bytes of the IRQ dispatch vector at $0314/$0315.

Disable the CIA interrupt sources, select $35 at the CPU port, install the IRQ entry at $0851, schedule $086D for raster value zero, clear the high raster-compare bit and enable the VIC raster interrupt before returning with interrupts enabled.
Save A, X and Y; inspect the stacked status and dispatch BRK through $0316 or IRQ through $0314.

Select VIC bank 1 and the character display settings, enable multicolour sprites, wait on the raster state, and write sprite positions. It then uses $801A to select a sprite; if its pointer is not $03 and its Y plus $11 is in the range $3C–$F5, it copies twelve bytes from each of two computed sprite addresses to $4033 and $4000, patches the split handler operands and schedules $0922 at Y plus $15. Otherwise it schedules $094E at $F9. The code uses eight-bit arithmetic for these tests.

Acknowledge the interrupt, set the selected sprite's Y and pointer from operands patched by $086D, wait until the raster passes a second Y value, then replace that sprite pointer with the other patched value. Continue to $0942 to schedule the later handler.
Schedule the handler at $094E for raster value $F9, then restore the interrupt registers and return.

Change the display settings, initialize sprite enable, multicolour, coordinates, colours and pointer bytes, call the sound update, and schedule $086D for raster value $0A. It then prepares room sprites before restoring the interrupt registers and returning.
Wait for 28 transitions through the high raster bit, then wait for the joystick fire bit at CIA port A to be released and pressed. Tail-call the sound-state clear routine.
Disable interrupts, clear sound and initialize selection 2. Pass the text pointer $0B4C to the outcome renderer at $0BE1.
Disable interrupts, clear sound and initialize selection 2. Pass the text pointer $0AD4 to the outcome renderer at $0BE1.

With phase zero, $A2F9 advances a five-by-five animation into phase 1; otherwise $A2F1 copies a reverse bitmap byte every 16 calls and walks the four source/destination operands back by three. Compare actor Y at $FC19 with target Y at $A30E. Equality sets $A312. Compare $804C with $A30F. If they differ, choose the $A434 path when $804C is 1 and the $A454 path otherwise. If $FC11 equals $A30D and $FC09 equals $A30C, set $A313 to 1 and return. If the high bytes match but the low bytes differ, choose the $A454 path when $FC09 is lower and the $A434 path otherwise. If the high bytes differ, choose the $A454 path when $FC11 is zero and the $A434 path otherwise. Each path sets $A2E4 and conditionally calls another helper when $A2E3 is nonzero.
Copy the saved three-byte scene actor position at $A2DC-$A2DE into $FC0A/$FC12/$FC1A.

When $A2DA is zero, select blank pointer 3 at $FC2A and return. Otherwise check the active position against the grid and both player positions, then dispatch state $A2E2 values 1, 2, 3 or 4 to $A833, $A7DA, $A8E5 or $A88C respectively.

Subtract 12 from the 16-bit position at $A2DC/$A2DD and divide its low byte by 8 for a column. Subtract $32 from $A2DE with byte wrap and divide by 8 for a row. Use that row to select a screen-row address at $8428, add the column, and add 31 if the adjusted position high byte is nonzero. Add $AC to the resulting address high byte with ADC, retaining the carry from the preceding high-byte addition; if $804E is nonzero, add 4 to that high byte with carry cleared. Patch the load at $A9B9 to this address. If the loaded byte is 1, clear $A2DA. This resembles the grid check at $9321, but that routine clears carry before adding $AC; the meaning of the active state remains open.
Call the active-position overlap check at $A9D5 with X and Y both zero, then again with X equal to 1 and Y equal to 2; return.

Return unless $804A,X equals $804E and $A2DA is nonzero. Halve the 16-bit positions at $A2DC/$A2DD and $FC05/$FC0D,Y, retain their low bytes, and test whether the first plus 3 is at least the second and less than the second plus 7, using eight-bit comparisons. Also require $A2DE to be at least $FC15,Y plus 1 and below $FC15,Y plus $16. On a match, call the first overlap dispatcher when X is not 1 or the second when X is 1, in a loop that starts Y at 9 and decrements it after each call. Then start sound effect $19 and clear $A2DA. The gameplay identity of the compared objects remains open.

Clear target-alignment flags $A312/$A313 and advance the random byte. Prefer the first or second player's coordinates according to its low bit, but skip a player whose state is 4 when the other branch is available. Save that player's X low/high and Y at $A30C-$A30E and its room at $A30F.
Store A, X and Y as target X low, X high and Y at $A30C-$A30E, clear $A311 and return.

Check placement overlap, advance $A2E8 and increment path index $A2E7 every fourth call. Read a direction byte into $A2D9 and dispatch values 1-4 with X=0 to the four actor movement routines.

Select sprite $6A when X is zero or $6E otherwise, and a paired pointer cycling through $38-$3F. Move actor Y down one and X right twice. Every fourth call through shared counter $A2E9, advance the paired-pointer operand and wrap $40 to $38.

Select sprite $68 when X is zero or $6C otherwise, and a paired pointer cycling through $28-$2F. Move actor Y up one and X right twice. Every fourth call through shared counter $A2E9, advance the paired-pointer operand and wrap $30 to $28.

Select sprite $69 when X is zero or $6D otherwise, and a paired pointer cycling through $48-$4F. Move actor Y up one and X left twice. Every fourth call through shared counter $A2E9, advance the paired-pointer operand and wrap $50 to $48.

Increment actor Y at $FC19 and return.

Clear $8046, $947E, $9485 and $8048; set $8047 to $C5, $8049 to $A5 and $804D to 1; then call the museum screen setup routine and return.

Increment the counter at $A2F7. When it reaches 5, clear it and increment $A2F8. For $A2F8 values 1 through 4, use it as an index into $C674 and $C679 and write the results to $FC29 and $8018. Increment $A2F2 and continue at $A62E until it reaches 8. Then clear it and copy one byte through the self-modified source operand at $AE9F to the destination operand at $AEA2. Increment $A2FB and return unless it reaches 5. Then clear it and increment $A2FC. Values below $16 enter $AF7A to select paired sprite pointers. Use Y as an index into the tables at $A31A and $A330, writing the selected pointers to $FC29 and $8018. If voice 3 has no active effect, start effect $14. Pass X=2 and Y=1 to the shared story-restoration routine. Adjacent entries pass Y=2 and Y=0 with the same episode index.

The selected path writes values to $FC25/$FC26 indexed by $B356, calls movement helpers and advances a four-update animation counter at $8040; the animation's next value is kept in the immediate operand of the path's load instruction.

Add $B358 to the selected low X byte at $FC05,Y and propagate the carry into $FC0D,Y, saving the result at $805F/$8061. Add $B359 to the selected Y byte at $FC15,Y and save it at $8060. Select the up-movement implementation from $B357: zero enters the $FC05/$FC15 pair path at $B750, while nonzero jumps to the $FC07/$FC17 pair path at $BC0E.

Low operand byte of the screen-cell load at $B7CC, formed from the selected row and column by $B752. The continuation compares the cell with $40, resolves the $A2E4 request and otherwise enters the up-movement path.
High operand byte of the screen-cell load at $B7CC; the setup subtracts $34 from the row-address high byte and adds 4 for the alternate room.

The saved code at $B7FB jumps to $B833, over this block. Select the down-movement implementation from $B357: zero enters the first sprite-pair path at $B849, while nonzero jumps to $BCD8.

Low operand byte of the screen-cell load at $B8E2. The continuation tests the selected code against $40, resolves the $A2E4 request and otherwise reaches the downward movement limit.

Low operand byte of the screen-cell load at $B9DB. Its continuation tests the cell against $40, resolves an active $A2E4 request and otherwise reaches the left-movement and room-crossing path.
High operand byte of the screen-cell load at $B9DB, patched by $B961 for the selected room.

The saved code at $BA0A jumps to $BA42, over this block. A match returns before the movement code at $BA42; a failed comparison branches to that movement code. Arithmetic is eight-bit. Whether another path enters this block remains open.
Select the right-movement implementation from $B357: zero enters the first sprite-pair path and nonzero jumps to the second-pair path.

Probe the sprite pair selected by Y at offsets ($20,$28). Codes below $40 permit right movement; an active $A2E4 request receives flags instead of moving. The captured branch bypasses the overlap block. Add 2 to the paired 16-bit X positions, except that room zero switches to room one when the high X byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $3A, redrawing at X=$0040. Low operand byte of the screen-cell load at $BB30. Its continuation tests the cell against $40, resolves the $A2E4 request and otherwise reaches the right-movement and room-crossing path.
High operand byte of the screen-cell load at $BB30, patched by $BAB6 for the selected room.

The saved code at $BB5F jumps to $BBA4, over this block. Low operand byte of the cell load at $BD71, patched by the second-pair down probe; its continuation compares the code with $40 before movement.
High operand byte of the second-pair down cell load, adjusted for the current room.

The saved code at $BD79 jumps to $BDB1, over this block. Set the current and second character's room bytes $8041 and $804B to 1, set both low X bytes at $FC07–$FC08 to $40 and both high bytes at $FC0F–$FC10 to zero, then call the screen setup at $8396.
Add two to the 16-bit X value at $FC07/$FC0F, duplicate the resulting low and high bytes at $FC08 and $FC10, and return.

Increment $C00B. At $2A, clear it and call the four reverse status-bitmap routines at $C0C4, $C16F, $C21A and $C2C5.
Dispatch first-player state $8026 values 0, 1, 2 and 3 to $C06C, $C117, $C1C2 and $C26D. Other values return unchanged.

Select a routine from $8027: values 0, 1, 2 and 3 jump to $C06C, $C117, $C1C2 and $C26D respectively. Other values return. The selected routines alter sprite-buffer bytes; their visual meaning remains open.

Status bitmap 1. Return if the low reverse-source operand at $C178 equals $80. Otherwise copy one byte from the reverse source to its sprite destination, subtract three from the forward source and both destination operands, and set the reverse source to the new forward source minus $3D.

Read the value at $8027. Values 1, 2 and 3 jump to $C42B, $C4E0 and $C595 respectively; any other value returns. The indexed overlap check at $9F52 calls this path when X is not 1 and its position tests match.

Examine the low byte of the load operand at $C384. If it is $FC, set $C319 to 1 and return. Select player-pair offsets in $C672/$C673 from $8042. On the first call after $801C is cleared, load the selected HUD state and pointer pair and advance $8025.
